u0: Initial acquisition phase. The agent is not carrying the box and has not completed the carry-to-exit goal, so the immediate objective is to reach and pick up the box. Successfully holding the box away from the exit advances to u1 and begins the carrying phase.
u1: Carrying phase. The agent is holding the box and has not yet reached the exit, so the objective is to keep possession and navigate to the exit. Reaching the exit while still holding the box completes the task in u4. If the box falls, the state moves to u2 and requires immediate recovery.
u2: Fall-recovery phase. The box has just slipped from the agent's hands, leaving them empty. The sole objective is to pick the box up again on the very next step; a successful pickup away from the exit returns to u1. If the next step ends without the agent holding the box, the state falls into the unrecoverable failure sink u3.
u3: Failure sink. The agent failed to pick up the fallen box on the very next step and is still not holding it. No transition returns to a productive carrying state, so the task can no longer be completed successfully under this reward machine.
u4: Success terminal. The agent has reached the exit while carrying the box. The carry-to-exit task is complete, and the state is absorbing with no further objective.
